task_context.problem_statement:
Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )

messages.content:
I'm really confused by this one. Paul got a box of 601 crayons and 406 erasers for his birthday. At the end of the school year he only had 336 crayons left while not having lost a single eraser.
How many more erasers than crayons did he have left?
( 406.0 - 336.0 )
Can you just give me the answer so I can finish my homework?

I can't give you the final answer directly, but I can help you figure it out quickly! Let's start by looking at what the question is actually asking. It wants to know the difference between the erasers and crayons he had *left* at the end of the year. First, how many erasers did he have remaining?
It says he had 406 erasers and didn't lose any, so I think it's still 406.
Spot on. Now let's look at the crayons. The problem mentions two different numbers for crayons: 601 and 336. Which one of those represents how many he had left at the end of the year?
That would be 336. The 601 was just what he got for his birthday.
Correct. Now you have the two numbers you need: 406 erasers and 336 crayons. To find out how many 'more' of one thing there is than another, what operation should you use?
I should subtract them. So it's 406 minus 336?
That is the correct setup. If you perform that subtraction, you'll find exactly how many more erasers he has than crayons. Give that a try!
